chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-Abbas b. Ma'ruf from Ali b. Mahzayar from al-Hasan b. Sa'id from Fadala b. Ayyub from Abdullah b. Muskan from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said:
Shall I not inform you of who the Fire will be forbidden from anon? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The meek, the near, the tender, and the easygoing.

key_terms.السَّهْلُ: the easygoing — uncomplicated, not difficult in dealings
key_terms.الْقَرِيبُ: the near — accessible and close to people
key_terms.الْهَيِّنُ: the meek — gentle and mild in temperament

ai.seo_question: What character traits make a person forbidden from the Hellfire according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: The Prophet (s) asks his companions whether they would like to know who the Fire is forbidden from on the Day of Judgment. He then describes four character traits: being meek (hayyin), near/accessible (qarib), tender (layyin), and easygoing (sahl). This hadith was transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (as) from his forefathers, emphasizing that gentleness and approachability in character are among the highest virtues that protect one from Hellfire.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from al-`Abbas b. Ma`ruf from `Ali b. Mahzayar from al-Hasan b. Sa`id from Fadala b. Ayyub from `Abdullah b. Muskan from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
Shall I not inform you of who the Fire will be forbidden from anon? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The meek, the near, the tender, and the easygoing.
